Field: Biology / 05/BIOS-02 Fisiologia vegetale

PMs are potential targets for improving crop performance: efficient dissipation of excess energy can enhance tolerance to abiotic stress, but excessive activation can unpair growth. Understanding the molecular basis ofPMs is therefore essential for optimizing light use in crops. item.title: Incarico di ricerca: Pica Code IR-2026-115 - Identification and functional characterization of extracellular vesicles involved in the pathophysiology of Alzheimer’s Disease: focus on miRNAs as inflammatory modulators and biomarkers (Univ. MODENA e R. E.)
item.description:
Deadline: 2026-11-27 13:00
Institution: Univ. MODENA e R. E., Modena
Field: Biology / 05/BIOS-06 Fisiologia

The project aims to investigate the role of extracellular vesicles (EVs) in neuron–microglia communication during the early stages of Alzheimer’s disease. The candidate will isolate EVs from mouse brain tissue and assess their effects on primary neural and glial cultures. The cultures will be examined using immunofluorescence, mitochondrial activity assays, and western blotting. EVs will also be administered to healthy animals to investigate their effects on neuroinflammation in vivo. Specifically, microglial and astrocytic activation will be assessed by immunofluorescence, while inflammatory marker expression will be evaluated using western blotting and cytokine assays.

item.title: Incarico di ricerca: 2026-IdrDip-05-medmol - Nuclear Signalling Compartmentalization in Skeletal Muscle Aging: the Role of Kinase/Phosphatase Imbalance (Univ. PAVIA)
item.description:
Deadline: 2026-11-25 12:00
Institution: Univ. PAVIA, Pavia
Field: Biology / 05/BIOS-06 Fisiologia

This project proposes the novel idea that the balance between nuclear kinases and phosphatases is crucial for skeletal muscle homeostasis during aging. To test this hypothesis, the candidate will use different techniques and novel tools (e.g., pooled optical CRISPR -FRET screenings, nuclear-targeted biosensors, spatial proteomics of nuclei in single fibers). The identification of new targets involved in age-related nuclear dysfunction and the conceptual idea that reframes sarcopenia as a nuclear signalling disorder, will be important to advance the knowledge in the field of aging.
